import { Backpack, FileCode, MonitorSmartphone } from 'lucide-react';

Configure your local SVM tooling to send commands to Gorbagana instead of a Solana cluster.

## Requirements

Install the tools you need for your workflow.

| Tool | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Solana CLI | Configure RPC, check balances, deploy programs |
| Rust | Build native SVM programs |
| Anchor | Build and test Anchor programs |
| Node.js | Run TypeScript clients and app tooling |

Use the official Solana and Anchor install guides for tool installation. These docs focus on the Gorbagana-specific values you need after the tools are installed.

## Configure RPC

Set Gorbagana as the active RPC endpoint.

<Tabs items={["CLI", "TypeScript"]}>
<Tab>

```bash
solana config set --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Check your active config:

```bash
solana config get
```

The `RPC URL` value should show the Gorbagana endpoint.

</Tab>
<Tab>

```ts
import { Connection } from "@solana/web3.js";

export const connection = new Connection(
  "https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf",
  "confirmed",
);
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Check a wallet balance

Use the CLI to check a wallet after you bridge or receive GOR.

```bash
solana balance
```

To check another address, pass it explicitly:

```bash
solana balance WALLET_ADDRESS
```

## Install the TypeScript client

Install `@solana/web3.js` when your app or script needs to read accounts, create transactions, or submit signed transactions.

<Tabs items={["npm", "pnpm", "yarn", "bun"]}>
<Tab>

```bash
npm install @solana/web3.js
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```bash
pnpm add @solana/web3.js
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```bash
yarn add @solana/web3.js
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```bash
bun add @solana/web3.js
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
